title: 7 Reasons To Upgrade Your Gas Furnace To Electric
desc: Interested in knowing seven reasons to upgrade your gas furnace for an electric one? Get all the answers from the experts at Rosenberg!

blocks.text: Electric furnaces offer a modern solution to many of the problems associated with gas furnaces. They are clean, reliable, and sustainable because they do not have to burn fuel to heat your home. If you need to replace an old furnace, you should consider upgrading to an electric model to take advantage of those benefits. In many cases, it can even make sense to replace a gas furnace that still works. Every home is unique, so we encourage you to learn more about electric furnaces and make an informed decision.
1. Fire Prevention

Gas furnaces can be fire hazards. While heating fires have been getting rarer for several decades, furnaces are still a leading cause of house fires. Gas furnaces are relatively safe if you take care of them, but many people neglect their heaters. For example, it is vital to change the filter in a gas furnace every few months. If you do not replace it, the dirty filter will increase the risk of a fire.

Electric furnaces avoid that problem by relying on electric heating elements. They do not introduce flammable materials into your home or create flames. That makes them the perfect choice for homeowners who want to be as safe as possible.
2. Reduced Air Pollution

Indoor air pollution is a major health problem for most people. Modern buildings often suffer from poor ventilation, which makes it easy for air pollution to build up to dangerous levels. Unfortunately, we spend a lot of time indoors, which exposes us to air pollution. Gas furnaces contribute to the problem.

Gas furnaces create several byproducts when they burn fuel. The most dangerous pollutant is carbon monoxide. It is highly poisonous and flammable, but it is also odorless and invisible. Your furnace should vent the carbon monoxide out of your home, but it can leak out of the system. If there is a problem, your home’s carbon monoxide detectors should warn you. Unfortunately, they can also fail. Carbon monoxide poisoning kills hundreds of people every year.

While carbon monoxide is the most serious problem, gas furnaces do release other pollutants. Their byproducts include nitrogen dioxide, formaldehyde, and particulates. All of those pollutants can harm you. They cause respiratory problems, headaches, and skin irritation. Some evidence also suggests they can interfere with your mental health and reduce your ability to focus.

That pollution is inherent to combustion. Any heater that burns fuel will produce these byproducts. Good ventilation and air purifiers can counteract the pollution, but they are not perfect. If you want to avoid them entirely, you need to stop using appliances that burn gas. When you replace your gas furnace with an electric model, you are eliminating one of the biggest sources of air pollution in your home. It will have a significant impact on your physical and mental health.
3. Sustainability

Sustainability is a growing concern for many people in our area. When we think about sustainability, we often think about driving habits, water usage, and waste. It is common to overlook the impact of our heating systems, but that is a mistake. Heating and cooling make up a huge percentage of the average home’s energy usage. If you want to go green, you should make sure that your furnace is as efficient as possible.

That usually means choosing an electric furnace. They often use less energy than traditional furnaces. That reduces your carbon emissions and your power bill. They can also offer additional environmental benefits in some homes. For example, you can combine an electric heater with solar panels. That ensures that the electricity for the furnace comes from a renewable source.

Sustainability will be particularly important if you expect to sell your home in the near future. Many modern shoppers prefer to buy homes that have green features. An electric furnace will make your home more appealing to buyers. It may help you sell your home quickly, and it is likely to increase your home’s value.
4. Durability

Electric furnaces are significantly more reliable than combustion systems. While they do have some moving parts, they are simpler than gas furnaces. You can expect an electric furnace to suffer from fewer mechanical problems than a comparable gas furnace. They also have a longer lifespan. Electric furnaces have a life expectancy of two or three decades, which is almost twice as long as gas furnaces.

That long lifespan contributes to their environmental benefits. All manufacturing processes consume energy. We use even more energy when we ship and install a new furnace. In the long run, you can save energy by using your furnace for as long as possible.
5. Space Efficiency

Small buildings usually benefit from an electric furnace because they are compact systems. They conserve space that you can use for other appliances or storage. Gas furnaces also need venting systems to remove toxic gas from your home. Those systems can waste a lot of space and make your home feel cramped.
6. Easy Automation

Home automation systems are common, and they are likely to get more popular as technology improves. If you expect to install smart control systems in your home, you should choose an electric furnace. They are much easier to automate than traditional gas furnaces. That will save time and money if you decide to upgrade your home with smart systems in the future.

Those systems offer several important benefits to the average homeowner. For example, they can reduce your energy consumption. Many modern smart systems can track your furnace usage. They use that information to calculate a heating plan that uses as little energy as possible. Automated systems also ensure that you never waste energy by forgetting to turn your furnace off.

They can also make your home more comfortable. You can control smart systems with a phone, which makes it easy to adjust your home’s temperature. Electric furnaces are precise systems, so you can always keep your home at the perfect temperature.
7. Quiet Operation

Gas furnaces can be noisy. They produce a loud rushing sound whenever the burner ignites. They also tend to make loud noises when they have mechanical problems. Electric furnaces are much quieter. They never ignite, which eliminates the rushing sound. Their reliability ensures that they have fewer noisy mechanical problems. They are a perfect choice for homeowners who want a serene and peaceful house.
